sections.title: Context7 as a complementary tool
sections.body:
Per MCP.Directory comparison (2026): Context7's Private Docs MCP is a paid hosted remote MCP for private, version-pinned documentation context, source citations, and stale-doc checks. DeepWiki indexes whole repos; Context7 indexes version-specific framework/library docs (React 19, Pydantic v2, Next.js 15). These are complementary, not competing — Devin/DeepWiki for repo understanding, Context7 for framework API docs.

For the fleet's private-repo code intelligence use case, the decision axis is: cloud-hosted simplicity (Devin MCP Pro $20/mo, code content sent to Cognition) vs local-first sovereignty (deepwiki-open self-hosted on Aegis, code never leaves infra, no ACU metering, but requires MCP wrapper + maintenance).

sections.title: Recommendation
sections.body:
Two viable paths confirmed by live research:
1. Devin MCP Pro ($20/mo): fastest path to private-repo DeepWiki with MCP integration; code content sent to Cognition's cloud — a partial counter-signal to the fleet's local-first architecture principle (memory holographic fact #0.5: Jack prefers research-first execution and local-first infra where possible).
2. deepwiki-open (self-hosted on Aegis): architecturally aligned (local-first, zero-cost, zero-cloud-dependency); requires ~1-2h setup and a custom MCP wrapper to expose the same tool surface (ask_question, read_wiki_structure, read_wiki_contents) that fleet agents expect.
A hybrid is viable: Devin MCP for initial evaluation, migrate to deepwiki-open if usage justifies the infra investment. No decision required in this heartbeat — this is a research deliverable only.
